title: Add byte-offset indexing for random file access

state.decision_rationale: Rejected absent a measured seek bottleneck. A consumer can build an offset map during one strict parse; in-band offsets add model-irrelevant entropy and serialization feedback, while a future tool-owned sidecar needs no core protocol change.

provenance.source_label: Claude Fable critique 7: no random access
provenance.review_target: Reported 39479-line MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Add offset= per index entry so a tool can seek directly to any file without parsing the entire packet and the index becomes a true table of contents.
feedback.normalized_claim: Index records should optionally identify exact serialized byte spans so seekable consumers can retrieve file bodies without scanning preceding content.

current_behavior: The index records source byte counts and line counts but not serialized packet offsets or body lengths.
The reference parser scans for each @file marker in manifest order, then consumes exact chunk byte counts.

Offsets depend on canonical packet encoding and exact prefix serialization, and putting variable-width offsets in the leading index creates a length-feedback problem that needs a deterministic layout or fixed-point algorithm.
Sidecar manifests could carry offsets without changing the in-band index prefix.

proposal.summary: Evaluate an optional seek table, either in-band with a canonical offset-width strategy or as a bound sidecar or trailer, using UTF-8 byte offsets into exact packet bytes.
candidate_changes: Define offset origin, addressed marker, length, encoding, and whether aliases have bodies.
Compare leading fixed-width offsets, a trailing seek table, and manifest-sidecar offsets.
Bind the seek table to packet identity so stale offsets are detectable.
Add direct-seek tests for multibyte text, CRLF, aliases, numbered projections, and large packets.
non_goals: Do not call source bytes an offset into the serialized packet.
Do not add offsets before canonical encoding and serialization are defined.
Do not require random-access metadata in model-only profiles where it adds cost without utility.

questions: Should offsets point to @file, @content, first payload byte, or a complete file span?
Is a trailing or sidecar table acceptable for consumers that want index-first navigation?
What packet sizes make seek offsets faster than one linear parse plus an in-memory map?
risks: Line-ending conversion or transcoding invalidates offsets.
In-band offset width can create unstable self-referential index lengths.
Offsets add maximum-entropy numbers that models do not need.
evidence_needed: Seek latency benchmarks by packet size and storage medium.
Canonical layout prototypes for leading, trailing, and sidecar tables.
Tampered and stale offset-table rejection tests.
